name: Counting Without Listing
lesson: If one choice has 3 options and the next has 4, there are $3\times4=12$ combined choices. A tree diagram can make the choices visible.
Ask whether order matters. Choosing two friends for a team is different from choosing a captain and a deputy. When a count lists each choice more than once, divide by the number of repeats.
A shortest grid route can be encoded as a sequence of right and up moves. Counting routes becomes a question about choosing the positions of those moves.

problems.q: You have 3 shirts and 2 hats. How many outfits use one shirt and one hat?
problems.hint: Match each shirt with each hat.
problems.solution: Each of the three shirts has two choices of hat, giving $3\times2=6$ outfits.

problems.q: A code has three digits. Each digit is either 0 or 1, and 000 is allowed. How many codes are possible?
problems.hint: There are two choices in each position.

problems.q: Four different children stand in a line. How many orders are possible?
problems.hint: There are fewer children available at each successive position.

problems.q: Choose two different toppings from five available toppings. The order does not matter. How many pairs can be chosen?
problems.hint: Choosing first and second counts each pair twice.
problems.solution: There are $5\times4=20$ ordered choices. Each pair appears in two orders, giving $20\div2=10$ pairs.

problems.q: On this grid, travel from A to B using only one-edge steps right or up. How many routes are possible?
problems.hint: Every route has three right steps and two up steps.
problems.solution: Choose the two positions for up steps among five positions. There are $5\times4\div2=10$ choices.
problems.imageAlt: A rectangular grid three edges wide and two edges high, with A at the bottom-left corner and B at the top-right.

problems.q: How many two-digit numbers can be formed from 1, 2 and 3 without repeating a digit?
problems.hint: Choose the tens digit, then the units digit.
problems.solution: There are 3 choices for the tens digit and 2 remaining choices for the units digit, giving 6 numbers.

problems.q: How many four-digit numbers use each of the digits 0, 1, 2 and 3 exactly once?
problems.hint: The first digit cannot be zero.
problems.solution: There are 3 choices for the first digit, then 3, 2 and 1 for the remaining digits. The total is $3\times3\times2\times1=18$.

problems.q: Six friends each shake hands with every other friend exactly once. How many handshakes occur?
problems.hint: Each handshake involves a pair of friends.
problems.solution: Counting five handshakes per person gives 30, but each handshake is counted twice. The total is $30\div2=15$.

problems.q: Five different finalists compete for gold, silver and bronze. There are no ties. How many medal assignments are possible?
problems.hint: The medals are different roles, so order matters.
problems.solution: There are 5 choices for gold, 4 for silver and 3 for bronze: $5\times4\times3=60$.

problems.q: How many rectangles of all sizes are formed by the grid lines in this 2-row, 3-column grid?
problems.hint: A rectangle is determined by two horizontal lines and two vertical lines.
problems.solution: Choose two of the three horizontal lines in 3 ways and two of the four vertical lines in 6 ways. The total is $3\times6=18$.
problems.imageAlt: Rectangular grid with two rows and three columns of equal cells.

problems.q: A shortest grid route uses exactly four right steps and three up steps. How many different routes are there?
problems.hint: Choose the three positions occupied by up steps.
problems.solution: There are $7\times6\times5$ ordered choices of up-step positions. Divide by $3\times2\times1$ to ignore their order: $210\div6=35$.

problems.q: How many integers from 1 to 100 contain the digit 7 at least once?
problems.hint: Count units-digit 7 and tens-digit 7, then account for the overlap.
problems.solution: There are 10 numbers with units digit 7 and 10 with tens digit 7. The number 77 belongs to both groups, so the total is $10+10-1=19$.
